title: Frederick II to Louis Michell (London), Berlin 28 Dec 1751, KHA Prins Willem V inv. 198 (DECODE R1957; sibling ministerial rescript R1955)

steps.what: Fetched DECODE R1957 and R1955 images with the cookie.
R1957 transcribed from both pages: clear opening and 550 code groups (transcription.txt, ct.txt).
Politische Correspondenz vol. 8 on archive.org searched by date: no. 5263 to Michell, 28 Dec 1751, opens with R1957's clear opening word for word.
anchors.py: repeated groups fall in the print's order at matching relative positions (1064 Vienne x4, 4310 Sardaigne x3, 3042 dessein, 545 avec, 4364 faire, 87 encore); 550 groups for 438 words.
R1955 (the other letter of the same date, ministerial rescript) transcribed in full: 362 groups.
R1955 vs R1957: 19 shared distinct groups, chance collisions; 296 distinct in 362, commonest group 5 times: large homophonic code with nothing for ciphertext-only analysis.
Printed or online decipherment of R1955 sought; the ministerial rescripts are not in the Politische Correspondenz; none found.
DECODE R1953 (von der Hellen to the King, 4 Jan 1752) checked as a sibling of R1955: different, smaller code.

WAINUT: six King-to-Michell letters in the cabinet code transcribed from Nationaal Archief 1.10.29 (Fagel) inv. 5177 scans 95-101 (1,813 groups; key1751/fagel5177/); their concepts are PC 8 nos. 5169, 5197, 5208, 5227, 5231, 5253.
WAINUT: the six letters aligned with their printed concepts; partial cabinet key v1, 72 entries (key1751/key_cabinet_v1_frozen.tsv), committed before R1957 was transcribed.

WAINUT: R1957 (548 groups; two corrections written above struck groups kept as notes) and R1955 (360 groups; one unsplit nine-digit run) transcribed independently from the DECODE images (key1751/R1957_tx.txt, R1955_tx.txt).

WAINUT blind test: R1957 decoded with frozen v1 before PC 5263 was consulted (181 of 548 groups); LCS of the 168 decoded whole words with PC 5263 = 123 against shuffle mean 58.9, max 65 (500 shuffles); 12 other PC letters to Michell at shuffle level; per group 142 confirmed, 9 partial, 6 contradicted, 24 not checkable; a hand check gives 150 confirmed and 6 contradicted, all from two wrong v1 entries (156, 4366_) (key1751/scripts/lcs_test.py, eval_blind.py).

WAINUT: R1957 aligned with PC 5263 (297 positions fixed by hand) and all seven letters re-aligned: cabinet key v2, 179 entries (122 A, 20 B, 37 C); 381 of 548 R1957 groups (69.5%) have a value (key1751/key_cabinet_v2_final.tsv, R1957_decipherment.tsv). Not tested on a held-out letter.
WAINUT: R1955 against the cabinet keys: v1 gives a value to 10 of 360 groups (2.8%), v2 to 20 (5.6%), against 181 of 548 (33.0%) and 381 (69.5%) for R1957: R1955 is not in the cabinet code.

WAINUT: table of Michell's envoy code (271 codes, 512 pairs) built from DECODE's transcriptions of the contemporary Dutch decipherments of Michell's reports R1050 and R1051 (key1751/scripts/envoy_key.py; table not committed); applied to R1955: 95 of 360 groups (26.4%) decoded; adjacent decoded words attested as French word pairs 19 of 30 against 11.1 for permutations (p = 0.001; with PC 8-9 only as corpus 14 vs 9.5, p = 0.046; the right v1 decode of R1957 scores only p = 0.28 on this test).

WAINUT circular-letter test, rule fixed in advance: LCS of R1955's 77 decoded words with each French PC 8-9 letter, z against 100 shuffles; best candidate (22 Dec 1751 - 10 Jan 1752) PC 5268 z = 2.69, highest control PC 5117 z = 4.85; no candidate qualifies; positive control finds a 17% word sample in its source at z 27.6-31.3 and in a 50% paraphrase at 5.8-10.9 (key1751/scripts/circular.py).

WAINUT prior-art check: this folder (Bourdeau, 19 Sep 2026) already matched R1957 to PC 5263 and transcribed R1955; the WAINUT match is an independent confirmation. A contemporary Dutch decipherment of R1955 may exist in Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inv. 159 (not digitised); not consulted.
WAINUT transcriptions compared with Bourdeau's (key1751/scripts/compare_tx.py): R1957 513 of 548 groups agree, 28 of 35 differences are 8 against 0; R1955 352 of 360 agree, 8 differences.

Review of PR #29 (Bourdeau with Claude Opus 5.5): blind test re-run on PC 8-9 rebuilt from our own archive.org OCR (LCS 121 vs shuffle mean 58.9, max 65; 12 controls at shuffle level); v2 coverage 381/548 confirmed; v1 LF hash matches frozen_keys.sha256 (time order rests on WAINUT's private history); Fagel 100R and 099R decoded with v2 follow PC 5227 and 5231 in order; our anchors 3042 (sur) and 169 (que) corrected; ct.txt corrected for 27 0/8 misreads, v2 coverage on it 357 -> 373 of 550.

outcome.method_basis: R1957's text is Politische Correspondenz 8 (1882) no. 5263, found during the attempt and matched to the Hague copy by the clear opening, length and positional anchors of repeated code groups; the code itself was not rebuilt. The sibling R1955 remains unread. Later contribution (WAINUT, 11 Oct 2026; outcome.parts): the cabinet code rebuilt from six Fagel 5177 letters and R1957 aligned with their printed concepts (179 entries, tested blind), and R1955 decoded in part with the contemporary Dutch decipherments of Michell's reports R1050/R1051.

parts.label: R1957 text, the printed concept matched to the Hague copy (Bourdeau)
parts.basis: PC 8 no. 5263 matched by clear opening, length and positions of repeated groups (Bourdeau, 19 Sep 2026); matched again independently by WAINUT, 11 Oct 2026.

parts.label: The King-to-Michell cabinet code of 1751 (WAINUT)
parts.records: DECODE R1957; Nationaal Archief 1.10.29 inv. 5177 scans 95-101
parts.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
parts.basis: 72 values from six Fagel 5177 letters aligned with their PC 8 concepts, tested blind on R1957 (LCS 123 against a shuffle maximum of 65); extended with R1957 to 179 values (122 grade A), which give a value to 381 of R1957's 548 groups (69.5%); no held-out test of the extended key.

parts.label: R1955 in Michell's envoy code (WAINUT)
parts.records: DECODE R1955; key material DECODE R1050, R1051
parts.method: read after matching with key from external sources
parts.basis: The contemporary Dutch decipherments of Michell's reports R1050/R1051 (271 code values, from DECODE's transcriptions) fit R1955: 95 of 360 groups (26.4%) decoded, adjacent decoded words coherent above chance (19/30 against 11.1, p = 0.001); fragments only.

gaps.item: R1955, the ministerial rescript of the same date (362 groups)
gaps.detail: Different large homophonic code; not in print; leads: Prussian ministerial code 1751 (GStA PK), Lyonet's decipherments, British decyphers of Michell's correspondence. WAINUT (11 Oct 2026): 95 of 360 groups decoded with the decipherments of Michell's reports R1050/R1051; the rest needs further decipherments of Michell's reports (probably KHA A31-1181, not online) or a contemporary decipherment of R1955 (possibly Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inv. 159, not digitised).

gaps.item: R1957 code table beyond the anchors
gaps.detail: A full alignment of the 550 groups to the print was not done; the text itself is known from the print. WAINUT (11 Oct 2026) aligned it: 179 key values, 381 of 548 groups with a value; the rest are mostly one-off syllables of spelled-out words and names.

outcome.notes: R1957's text is the printed minute (PC 8 no. 5263), identified here by clear opening, length and positional anchors; the code was not rebuilt, so no per-token reading and no fraction. R1955 is attempted, open. 'key confirms' refers to the positional anchors, not a full key. WAINUT contribution of 11-12 Oct 2026 (NOTES, key1751/): cabinet key rebuilt and tested blind, R1955 decoded in part; outcome.method, class, fraction_read and grades describe Bourdeau's primary result and were left unchanged; the parts carry the contribution.
